clue.text: Chased by Tom under the bed ?

definitions.meaning: the mouse forever pursued by the cat in the Tom and ... cartoons
an old British slang word for a chamber pot, kept under the bed

explanation.surface: Someone or something is pursued by a man called Tom and ends up hiding beneath the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, earthier sense: a jerry is British slang for a chamber pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the cartoon mouse who is the cat's quarry, and slang for a potty kept beneath a bed.

clue.text: Secret agent, seven centuries back

parts.note: seven centuries is 700; written backwards it gives the famous double-O-seven code number

explanation.surface: A spy from the Middle Ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' does not mean long ago: 700 written backwards is 007, Fleming's agent's number.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming's spy carries the code number 007.

clue.text: Governor provides aid for draughtsmen

definitions.meaning: a person who governs, such as a monarch
a straight-edge used in technical drawing

explanation.surface: A governor supplies drawing equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: one who reigns, and a measuring straight-edge used by those who draw plans.

clue.text: With which Moslems chopped up a nasty hag

definitions.text: With which Moslems chopped up a nasty hag

indicators.note: the words are cut up and their letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A grim scene of a hideous old woman hacked to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped up' rearranges A NASTY HAG; the whole clue also describes the curved Turkish sword.
explanation.definitionFit: The yataghan is a curved Turkish sabre, a weapon for chopping.

clue.text: It's very high, often, for a set entertainment

definitions.text: It's very high, often, for a set entertainment

parts.words: It's very high, often, for a set entertainment
parts.note: VHF, very high something, is the waveband a radio set is tuned to for its entertainment; 'often' hints at the word for how often a wave repeats

explanation.surface: Something tall and recurring is laid on as a staged entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' is the wireless set, not a stage set: VHF radio stands for very high frequency.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio broadcasts are carried on a wave measured by its rate of oscillation, very high for VHF stations.

clue.text: Suitable rise in food for highwayman

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the word for food
in a down clue, rising means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: suitable means apt

explanation.surface: Fitting that food prices go up for a robber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns APT upward to TPA, which goes 'in' FOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpad was a robber on foot, the walking counterpart of a mounted highway robber.

clue.text: Enjoys the blow out Henry included in expenses

indicators.note: Henry is placed inside the word for expenses

parts.note: exes is informal for expenses
Hal is a pet form of Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: Henry enjoys a lavish party and puts it on expenses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow-out' suggests a feast; read literally, one who breathes out has a good blow out.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe out is literally to blow out air, whimsically enjoying a blow.

clue.text: Ghost as uninvited guest

definitions.meaning: in ancient Rome, a guest brought along by an invited one

explanation.surface: A ghost turns up uninvited.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin word for shadow means both a shade of the dead and a hanger-on brought to dinner by an invited guest.

clue.text: Cancels out sinful lie

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone retracts a wicked untruth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cancels out' looks like the definition, but 'out' is the anagram signal on SINFUL LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul or void something is to cancel it.

clue.text: Yes, service is long

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes
RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Agreeing that the church service goes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' is a verb: to pine.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine or crave is to long for something.

clue.text: One must lose before growth of wisdom ?

definitions.text: One must lose before growth of wisdom ?

parts.words: One must lose before growth of wisdom ?
parts.note: a child sheds its first set of teeth long before the wisdom teeth come through

explanation.surface: A maxim that we must suffer losses before we grow wise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wisdom' means wisdom teeth, not sagacity; the thing lost is a child's first tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby tooth is shed in childhood, years before the last molars, named for wisdom, erupt.

clue.text: Wood that turns into a form of chocolate

indicators.note: the phrase 'that turns' tells us the chocolate piece is to be read from right to left

parts.note: chocolate is often sold as a slab

explanation.surface: A timber that magically becomes a bar of chocolate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses A SLAB as one run, giving the light timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light tropical timber used for models.

clue.text: A bit sheepish, namely, taking inferior paper

parts.note: SC abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely
a rag is a newspaper of poor quality

explanation.surface: Someone a little embarrassed picks up a down-market newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit sheepish' is literal: scrag is the bony neck end of mutton, a bit of a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: The scrag end is the cheap neck cut of a sheep's carcass.

clue.text: New Latin opus needs some beating

indicators.note: a new version of the words gives their letters freshly arranged

explanation.surface: A fresh Latin composition takes a lot of hard work to beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges LATIN OPUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is a rhythmic throb, so a sequence of throbbing is some beating.

clue.text: Wrong direction for in-patients ?

parts.note: patients admitted to hospital go into a ward; one heading out of the ward goes the other way

explanation.surface: Hospital patients are sent the wrong way down the corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as OUT WARD: the opposite place for someone meant to be in a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading away from the inside is the reverse of what an admitted patient should do.

clue.text: It's spread out on board, to surpass Bunter's expectation of tuck

parts.note: to top something is to surpass it
Billy Bunter, the greedy schoolboy of the Greyfriars stories, forever awaited a food parcel from home

explanation.surface: A school feast laid out on the table outdoes even Bunter's hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is British school slang for sweets and snacks; 'on board' means aboard ship, where top hamper is the rigging and gear above deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper rigging, spars and gear of a ship are spread out aloft on board.

clue.text: The fair Miss Severn

parts.note: Milton's Comus invokes the nymph of the River Severn as '... fair'

explanation.surface: A pretty young woman with the surname Severn.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn is Britain's longest river; in Milton's masque Comus its nymph is addressed in the song beginning '... fair, listen where thou art sitting'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin name for the River Severn is personified as a fair nymph in Milton.

clue.text: Drinks always a long time after opening of bar

indicators.note: the later pieces come after the first letter
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ever means always
ages is a long time

explanation.surface: A drinker is forever waiting for the pub to open.
explanation.definitionFit: Beverages are drinks of any kind.

clue.text: Self-confidence the object of policy

definitions.meaning: life cover is what an insurance policy buys

explanation.surface: Confidence is what a political policy aims to inspire.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: self-assurance, and life cover bought by a policy from an insurer.

clue.text: One's back in regimental HQ in earnest

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the regimental base

parts.note: a depot is a regiment's headquarters

indicators.note: the contraction is written from right to left

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I'S

explanation.surface: A soldier returns to headquarters in a serious mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IS to SI, which sits 'in' DEPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest is a pledge paid in advance, as is a down payment.

clue.text: Well content in Wonderland story

parts.note: at the Mad Hatter's tea party the Dormouse tells of three sisters living at the bottom of a well full of syrup

explanation.surface: Someone is perfectly happy in a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well content' looks like 'quite happy' but means what fills the well in the Dormouse's tale in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: The well in the Dormouse's story was full of this sticky syrup.

clue.text: Amends pay increases about point-five

indicators.note: the pay rises wrap around the other letters

parts.note: pay increases are rises
E is east, a compass point
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Someone corrects pay rises by roughly half a percent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point-five' looks like 0.5 but is two pieces: E, a compass point, and V, Roman five; RISES goes 'about' them.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise a text is to correct it.

clue.text: Stand another round and retire

explanation.surface: A drinker buys more drinks and then goes home.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: treating again, and withdrawing.

clue.text: Labyrinthine wonder?

parts.note: split the word as a maze plus ment: wonder that comes from a labyrinth

explanation.surface: A marvel of intricate design.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as A MAZE MENT, a labyrinth inside a word meaning wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonishment is wonder, and a labyrinth is a maze.

clue.text: A student member's rousing call

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A student union member makes a stirring appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' is a limb here, not a club member.
explanation.definitionFit: A wake-up signal rouses sleepers.

clue.text: Bunnies, topless, tail-less, crazy picture by Sickert

indicators.note: taking off the top and the tail leaves all but the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A risqué painting of nude playmates.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the first and last letters leaves UNNIE, which 'crazy' rearranges. Walter Sickert was an English painter; Ennui (c.1914) is one of his best-known works.
explanation.definitionFit: Sickert's painting of a bored couple bears this title, meaning listless weariness.

clue.text: No pedestrian problem in geometry

definitions.meaning: someone on horseback or a bike is not walking
in geometry, a supplementary problem following from a theorem

explanation.surface: A dull, plodding exercise in mathematics.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: one who travels mounted rather than on foot, and a follow-on exercise appended to a proof.

clue.text: Bridge contractor's stupid partner

parts.note: in contract bridge the declarer's partner lays the hand face up and takes no part in play

explanation.surface: A builder of bridges works with a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge contractor' is the declarer in contract bridge, not a builder.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the declarer's partner's exposed hand is played by the declarer, a silent partner.

clue.text: "Willows whiten, ——s quiver" (Tennyson)

parts.note: fill the blank from The Lady of Shalott, where the line names a tree beside the willows

explanation.surface: A quotation with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's The Lady of Shalott opens 'Willows whiten, aspens quiver'; the blank takes the tree, with the printed s making it plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The trembling poplar is famous for quivering leaves, named in Tennyson's line.

clue.text: Many of them work for a living

definitions.text: Many of them work for a living

parts.words: Many of them work for a living
parts.note: a living is a church benefice, the post a parish priest is appointed to

explanation.surface: Most people have to earn their keep.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Church of England a living is a parish post with its income, so priests literally work for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: Priests and vicars hold church livings.

clue.text: Provided by Jack Point or the Mikado's future prisoners

definitions.meaning: Jack Point is the jester in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Yeomen of the Guard, whose job is mirth
the Mikado sings that each prisoner pent shall represent a source of innocent fun

explanation.surface: A jester entertains the emperor's next batch of convicts.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Mikado's song 'A more humane Mikado', each prisoner is made to represent 'a source of innocent' fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of fun: what a jester supplies, and what the Mikado's convicts are made to provide.

clue.text: Manner makes man, said the Comte de Buffon

definitions.text: Manner makes man, said the Comte de Buffon

parts.words: Manner makes man, said the Comte de Buffon
parts.note: the French naturalist Buffon declared that a writer's manner of expression is the man himself

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat's maxim about manners.
explanation.walkthrough: Buffon's dictum in French is 'Le style est l'homme même'.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic manner of writing or doing is one's way, as Buffon said.
